correctness.rationale: For a Polish group G with ample generics, the Kechris–Rosendal automatic-continuity theorem applies to any abstract homomorphism into a separable target. If L is dense in G, continuity implies φ(G)⊂closure φ(L), while the reverse closure inclusion follows from L⊂G. Every finite set in φ(L) lifts to finitely many generators of the locally finite L, hence generates a finite group. If H is torsion-free, every φ(l)=1, and Hausdorffness of H forces φ(G)={1}. Siniora–Solecki supply precisely ample generics plus dense locally finite L for all stated free-homogeneous finite-relational M. Nonseparable targets and homomorphisms to non-Hausdorff torsion-free topological groups are outside scope.
residual_risks: No independent full reconstruction of the Kechris–Rosendal original proof; the published automatic-continuity theorem is used as an external lemma.
